scope: Proposition 8.1 (Approximate moves) of the manuscript “No percolation at criticality on quasi-transitive graphs” (preprints/No-percolation-at-criticality-on-quasi-transitive-graphs-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 213 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5929ccea200fd743), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let G be an infinite connected locally finite graph and let a group Λ act on it by automorphisms with finitely many vertex orbits. Let π : V (G) → Z2 be onto, with edge increments bounded in Euclidean norm by Dπ and with π(gx) = π(x)+ag, where g 7→ ag is an epimorphism from Λ to Z2. Suppose 0 < pc < 1 and, at pc, there is almost surely a unique infinite cluster and no infinite open ray with bounded π-projection. For every 0 < e, η < 1/10, there is an integer m such that for every requested ρ0 > 0 one can choose an invertible linear map Φ : R2 → R2 and a parameter p′ ∈ [pc/2, pc) with the following properties. The coordinates (t, z) = Φπ have edge increments at most ρ0 in supremum norm. For y ∈ V (G) and s ∈ {−1, 1}, let Es(y) be the event that an open path starts in B(y, m), stays within supremum coordinate distance 100 of y, and ends within supremum distance e/4 of (t(y) + 1, z(y) + s). Then Pp′ (Es(y)) ≥ 1 − η (y ∈ V (G), s ∈ {−1, 1}). The radius m is chosen before ρ0.
